福爾摩沙小導遊臺南 Tainan・東區

大東門The Great East Gate

這座城門掛著兩塊門牌，一塊朝外，一塊朝內。大東門是 1725 年府城動工時最早興建的城門之一：木造、帶樓臺。林爽文事件後，1788 年改以三合土重建為兩層城樓。它採歇山重簷屋頂、四周設廊道，更高、也更利防守。戰後的歲月對它並不溫柔：1955 年艾瑞絲颱風豪雨，城牆崩塌，壓毀鄰宅。1975 年市府整修城樓：紅柱、白牆、橙色燕尾屋頂。窗戶造型俏皮多變：卷軸形、扇形、方形、八角形。正式名稱是東安門，雅稱則是迎春門。朝東、朝城外的是「東安門」，朝西、朝城內的是「迎春門」。迎春禮中斷百年後，2017 年復辦。每年立春，市長要「鞭」一頭紙紮的春牛。春牛的尾巴長一尺二寸，一寸代表一個月。

This gate has two names on two signboards, one facing out and one facing in. The Great East Gate was among the first gates built when construction of the prefecture city began in 1725: wood, with a tower. After the Lin Shuang-wen rebellion, it was rebuilt in 1788 in lime-sand-clay as a two-story gatehouse. It has a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof and surrounding corridors, taller and far more defensible. The postwar years were unkind. In 1955, the rains of Typhoon Iris collapsed a stretch of wall onto neighboring homes. The city restored the gatehouse in 1975: red pillars, white walls, and an orange swallowtail roof. Its windows come in a playful variety of shapes: scroll, fan, square, and octagon. Its formal name is Dong'an Gate, but its poetic name is Yingchun Gate, the Gate of Welcoming Spring. Dong'an Gate faces east, out of the city, and Yingchun Gate faces west, into the city. The Welcoming Spring Ceremony was revived in 2017 after a century's pause. Every spring, the mayor whips a paper Spring Ox. The Spring Ox's tail is one foot two inches, one inch per month.

為什麼值得來

Why it matters & history

大東門是府城最早興建的城門之一，也是現存的府城城門之一。城門內外各掛一塊門牌：朝外「東安門」、朝內「迎春門」；每年立春的迎春禮，也在這裡重新上演。

The Great East Gate was one of the first gates built for the old city and still stands today. It carries two name boards: one facing out of the city and one facing in. Every spring the old welcome-spring rite is held here again.

  1. 1725府城動工時最早興建的城門之一，木造、帶樓臺。One of the first gates built for the city wall, made of wood with a tower.
  2. 1788林爽文事件後，以三合土重建為兩層城樓。After the Lin Shuangwen uprising, it is rebuilt as a two-story gatehouse.
  3. 1955艾瑞絲颱風豪雨使城牆崩塌。Heavy rain from Typhoon Iris brings down part of the wall.
  4. 1975市府整修城樓。The city restores the gatehouse.
  5. 2017中斷百年的立春迎春禮復辦。The spring welcome rite returns after a century.

認識景點

About the place

城樓：城門上方的建築。大東門有兩層城樓。 颱風：帶來豪雨的強烈風暴。1955 年艾瑞絲颱風讓城牆崩塌。 立春：在農業時代的台灣，立春這天要迎春、鞭春牛。 春牛：按神聖尺寸紮成的紙牛：高四尺、長八尺。

gatehouse: The building on top of a city gate. The Great East Gate has a two-story gatehouse. typhoon: A very strong storm with heavy rain. In 1955, the rains of Typhoon Iris collapsed part of the wall. the Beginning of Spring: In agricultural Taiwan, this day was marked by welcoming spring and whipping the Spring Ox. Spring Ox: A paper ox built to sacred measurements. It stands 4 feet tall and 8 feet long.

鞭子；鞭打：有握柄的長鞭。芒神的鞭長二尺四寸。 收成、豐收：收割的作物。迎春禮祈求風調雨順、五穀豐登。 芒神：掌管季節的牧童神。身高三尺六寸五分，對應一年 365 天。 門牌、匾額：寫著名字的牌子。朝東、朝城外是「東安門」，朝西、朝城內是「迎春門」。

whip: A long cord on a handle. The Mangshen's whip is 2 feet 4 inches long. harvest: The crops people gather. The ceremony prays for good weather and full harvests. Mangshen: The herdboy spirit of the seasons. He stands 3 feet 6.5 inches, for the 365 days. signboard: A board with a name on it. Dong'an Gate faces east, out of the city, and Yingchun Gate faces west, into the city.

圓環：車子繞圈行駛的圓形路口。大東門就站在圓環中央。 燕尾屋頂：屋脊兩端像燕子尾巴般翹起。大東門的燕尾屋頂是橙色的。 勒索：用威脅取得錢財。門洞裡的告示禁止衛兵勒索。 節氣：一年有 24 個節氣。鞭子一寸對應一個節氣。

roundabout: A round road where cars drive in a circle. The Great East Gate stands in the middle of one. swallowtail roof: A roof whose ends curve up like a swallow's tail. The gate's roof is orange. extortion: Taking money from people by threats. A notice in the tunnel forbids extortion by guards. solar term: There are 24 solar terms in a year. The whip has one inch for each solar term.

實景照片

Photos on site

迎春門 West side

這是大東門的兩層城樓。這一面朝西、朝向城內，白牆上的匾額寫著「迎春門」（由右往左讀），意思是「迎接春天的門」。下面是石塊砌成的拱形門洞。

This is the two-story gatehouse of the Great East Gate. This west side faces into the city, and the plaque on the white wall reads Yingchun Gate, the Gate of Welcoming Spring. Below it is an arch of stone blocks.

東安門 East side

這是大東門朝東、朝向城外的一面：城樓有紅柱、白牆，二樓有兩扇八角形的窗。拱門上方的石頭刻著它的正式名稱「東安門」。

This is the east side of the gate, facing out of the city. The gatehouse has red pillars, white walls, and two octagon windows upstairs. Above the arch, the stone is carved with its formal name, Dong'an Gate.

東安門石刻 Carved name

靠近看東面拱門上方：石頭上刻著「東安門」三個字，要由右往左讀。

Look closely above the arch on the east side. The words Dong'an Gate are carved into the stone. Read them from right to left.

示禁碑 The 1848 tablet

門洞裡的這塊石碑立於 1848 年（道光二十八年），是官府的禁令：農民、商人、小販和牛車經過城門時，守城的兵丁不准勒索他們的錢。

This stone tablet inside the gate dates from 1848. It is an official order: soldiers must not take money by threats from farmers, merchants, and hawkers passing through the gate.

春季石座（一） Spring block 1

城門前有四座石座，代表春夏秋冬。「春」字兩旁是兩條青龍；三位節氣神是立春、雨水、驚蟄。

Four stone blocks near the gate stand for the four seasons. On the Spring block, two green dragons guard the word Spring. The figures are the Beginning of Spring, Rain Water, and the Awakening of Insects.

春季石座（二） Spring block 2

春季石座的另一面：春分、清明、穀雨。

The other side of the Spring block shows the Spring Equinox, Clear and Bright, and Grain Rain.

夏季石座（一） Summer block 1

「夏」字兩旁是兩隻紅色的鳥；三位節氣神是立夏、小滿、芒種。

On the Summer block, two red birds stand by the word Summer. The figures are the Beginning of Summer, Grain Buds, and Grain in Ear.

夏季石座（二） Summer block 2

夏季石座的另一面：夏至、小暑、大暑。

The other side of the Summer block shows the Summer Solstice, Minor Heat, and Major Heat.

秋季石座（一） Autumn block 1

「秋」字兩旁是兩隻白老虎；三位節氣神是立秋、處暑、白露。

On the Autumn block, two white tigers guard the word Autumn. The figures are the Beginning of Autumn, the End of Heat, and White Dew.

秋季石座（二） Autumn block 2

秋季石座的另一面：秋分、寒露、霜降。

The other side of the Autumn block shows the Autumn Equinox, Cold Dew, and Frost's Descent.

冬季石座（一） Winter block 1

「冬」字旁是被蛇纏繞的烏龜（右邊那隻已經掉了）；三位節氣神是立冬、小雪、大雪。

On the Winter block, a turtle with a snake around it sits by the word Winter. The figures are the Beginning of Winter, Minor Snow, and Major Snow.

冬季石座（二） Winter block 2

冬季石座的另一面：冬至、小寒、大寒。每座石座兩面各三位，四座合起來正好是二十四節氣。在中國傳統裡，青龍、朱雀、白虎、玄武（龜蛇）分別代表春、夏、秋、冬。

The other side shows the Winter Solstice, Minor Cold, and Major Cold. Four blocks with six figures each make twenty-four solar terms. In Chinese tradition, the dragon, the red bird, the tiger, and the turtle with a snake stand for spring, summer, autumn, and winter.
